experiment: AUX-3 soft policy target (T=4, x8 weight, prune 0.02) vs hard (argmax, 1x) — 5^3, net@512 vs cls@48, 3 seeds, plain A3GoNet 64x6
data: distill_softpol_5cubed.npz (52901 ex, classical@128 teacher, raw visits)
note_top1: holdout top1/top3-vs-argmax favors HARD by construction (it IS the hard objective); not a fair policy-quality metric. Meaningful signals = strength + value-MSE.
verdict: Soft policy target gives a SMALL, CONSISTENT (all 3 seeds) strength edge (+2.9pp pooled) and BETTER value-MSE (all 3 seeds), but Wilson CIs OVERLAP -> NOT decisive. Neither arm beats classical at 5^3. Confirms with AUX-1: target/aux-representation tweaks give consistent-but-marginal gains; the 5^3 absolute-strength bottleneck is deeper (capacity/architecture/search), not the policy-target representation.
